get.description: Returns all Financial Period groups for the company, paginated by group. Groups are never split across pages and are ordered by their earliest period start date.

parameters.name: filters[from_date]
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound of the date window (ISO 8601 date, "YYYY-MM-DD"). When provided, only groups whose span ends on or after this date are returned. Groups are returned in full (all their periods), not only the periods inside the window. Optional; when omitted the window is unbounded below.

parameters.name: filters[to_date]
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound of the date window (ISO 8601 date, "YYYY-MM-DD"). When provided, only groups whose span starts on or before this date are returned. Groups are returned in full (all their periods), not only the periods inside the window. Optional; when omitted the window is unbounded above. Must be on or after `filters[from_date]` when both are given.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort groups by start date. `date` orders by earliest period start ascending (the default); `-date` orders descending.

name.description: Display name of the individual period within the group (e.g. "Q1 2026").

x-changelog.summary: Reduce pagination limits for GET Financial Periods
x-changelog.description: The maximum allowed per_page value has been reduced from 200 to 100, aligning this endpoint with the Procore REST v2 platform pagination maximum of 100 items per page; requests with per_page > 100 will now fail validation. The default per_page (used when the parameter is omitted) has been reduced from 50 to 10, so clients that do not pass per_page will receive fewer records per page. Use the Total and Per-Page response headers and paginate accordingly.

x-changelog.summary: Add date window filter and date sort to GET Financial Periods
x-changelog.description: The endpoint now accepts optional filters[from_date] and filters[to_date] query parameters defining an inclusive date window; a group is returned when its span overlaps the window, and qualifying groups are returned in full (all their periods). It also accepts an optional sort parameter (date or -date) to order groups by start date ascending or descending. Both bounds are optional and independent; when both are supplied, to_date must be on or after from_date.
